name: Connla’s Well

attributes.attribute: fed on the nuts of the well
found the well and paid with her life

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Connla's Well, also called the Well of the Maiden, is an Irish site of myth. No one knows for whom it is named, whether fairy or mortal. Its place is not known either, whether under the sea, in the Otherworld, or in a part of Ireland. Nine hazel trees hung over the water and dropped nuts into it. Fat salmon fed on the nuts, and each nut stained the fish with spots. Someone who ate the nuts, drank the water, or ate the salmon would win wisdom. The river goddess Beach she found the well and paid with her life for doing so.

okr.objective: Connla's Well is an Irish well that grants wisdom.
key_results: Nine hazel trees hung over the well.
Salmon fed and died the nuts.
The goddess Sinann found it and perished.
